diagnostic_evidence.quote: be a measurement matrix whose rows consist of randomly sampled independent sub-Gaussian vectors. Then, $\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\mat{A}$ satisfies $(\delta,\vr)$-TensorRIP over $\mathcal{S}_{r}^{CP}$

issues.failure_explanation: Both TensorRIP theorems (Theorems lem:trip_hosvd and theorem:trip_cp) are stated for rows that are merely independent sub-Gaussian vectors, with no isotropy (or i.i.d. unit-variance entries) requirement. Without such a normalization the conclusion is false (e.g. rows supported on a fixed proper subspace, or the zero matrix, are sub-Gaussian). The cited result of Rauhut et al. requires independent mean-zero unit-variance entries, and the proof of theorem:trip_cp via a covering/union argument likewise needs isotropic rows.

failure_location.quote: be a measurement matrix whose rows consist of randomly sampled independent sub-Gaussian vectors. Then, $\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\mat{A}$ satisfies $(\delta,\vr)$-TensorRIP

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that the rows are isotropic (or have i.i.d. mean-zero unit-variance sub-Gaussian entries) to both statements.
issues.overall_effect: As stated the two TensorRIP theorems are false; later uses (Theorem thm:main under Assumption 1, which does include isotropy) are not affected once the hypothesis is added.
issues.title: Invoked TensorRIP theorem stated without isotropy/variance normalization of rows
issues.why_classification: A standard missing hypothesis; adding it restores the cited results and all downstream uses already satisfy it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Further, since the chosen $m$ scales linearly with $n$, we also get that 
$
\mathbbm{P} (\mathcal{E}_1)\le cn^{-\phi}$ for some constant $c>0$.
For comparison, i.i.d. sub-Gaussian measurements are known to satisfy \eqref{eq:trim-rip} -- without any trimming --  for $m$ of the same order up to the logarithms and an additional $d$-factor

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the variance of $\langle a_{1j}\otimes\cdots\otimes a_{dj},x\rangle^2$ by $((4C)^{2d}-1)\|x\|^4$ and consequently obtains (via Lemma jl_trimming) the requirement $m\ge C^d\delta^{-2}\ln(4|\mathcal N|n^\phi)$, which contains a factor exponential in $d$ (genuinely present for Gaussian entries: the fourth moment of a product of $d$ standard Gaussians is $3^d$) and a term $\phi\ln n$ (also forced by $\alpha=n^{-\phi}\ge 4e^{-cm}$ and by $k=\ln(8n^\phi)<m$). The stated conditions (eq:order_m_hosvd), (eq:order_m_cp) have constants $C_1,C_2$ depending only on the sub-Gaussian norm and no $\phi$-dependence, so the statement is not what the proof supports (and is false for large $\phi$, where $k>m$). Similarly, $\mathbb P(\mathcal E_1)\le 2me^{-cn/d}\le cn^{-\phi}$ only holds with $c$ depending on $d$ and $\phi$ (or for $n$ large relative to $d,\phi$).

failure_location.quote: Here, $C_1, C_2$ and $c \in \R^{+}$ are constants that can depend on the sub-Gaussian norm of the entries of $\mat{A}_i$'s.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate (eq:order_m_hosvd),(eq:order_m_cp) with a $C^d$ factor and an additive $\phi\ln n$ term (and allow $c$ to depend on $d,\phi$), and weaken the comparison claim in the informal theorem accordingly; alternatively supply a sharper variance/trimmed-mean analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit $d$-dependence advertised in Theorem trim_trip and the informal comparison in thm:main-informal/footnote ('same order up to logarithms and an additional d-factor' versus i.i.d. sub-Gaussian measurements) are unsupported; for fixed $d$ and $\phi$ the qualitative result survives.
issues.title: Theorem trim_trip hides exponential-in-d and phi dependence of the sample complexity
issues.why_classification: The result survives for fixed $d$, but repairing it necessarily withdraws the advertised dimension dependence (exponential vs linear in $d$), a non-trivial quantitative weakening rather than a cosmetic fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\|\vu_{(k)} - \vv_{(k)}\| \leq \|\vu-\vv\|_\infty$ for any two vectors $\vu$ and $\vv$ and their $k$-th order statistics

issues.failure_explanation: The rows of $\mat A^{\vx}$ and $\mat A^{\hat\vx}$ are ordered by the absolute values $|a_i^T x|$, $|a_i^T\hat x|$, but the vectors $\mat A^{\vx}\vx$ and $\mat A^{\hat\vx}\hat\vx$ keep signs. The order-statistics lemma applies to sorted vectors, not to vectors sorted by magnitude with signs retained: e.g. $u=(1,-1.1)$, $v=(1.1,-1)$ have $\|u-v\|_\infty=0.1$ but the entries sorted by absolute value are $(1,-1.1)$ and $(-1,1.1)$, differing by 2. So the displayed inequality is false in general.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Run the decomposition with the entrywise absolute-value vectors $|\mat A^{\vx}\vx|$, $|\mat A^{\hat\vx}\hat\vx|$ (same norms), to which the order-statistics lemma applies with $\||Ax|-|A\hat x|\|_\infty\le\|Ax-A\hat x\|_\infty$.
issues.overall_effect: One step of the net argument for Theorem trim_trip is invalid as written; the conclusion is unaffected after repair since only norms are needed.
issues.title: Order-statistics inequality misapplied to signed vectors in the proof of Theorem trim_trip
issues.why_classification: A local, routine replacement argument preserves the theorem exactly.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the trimmed matrix at iteration $k$, $\mat{A}_k$ corresponds to $\mat{A}_{m_{trim}}^{\algoname{Vec}(\tX^k - \tX^*)}$ as per Definition~\ref{def:trimmed-matrix}

issues.failure_explanation: Line 4 of Algorithm 1 selects the $m_{trim}$ indices with smallest residual, so $|\Theta_k|=m_{trim}$ and the update rescales by $m/m_{trim}$. The surrounding text and (def:truncated-A) instead treat $\Theta_k$ as having $m-m_{trim}$ rows (removing the $m_{trim}$ most aligned rows, rescaled by $m/(m-m_{trim})$), as in Definition def:trimmed-matrix and as used in the experiments ($m_{trim}$ from 5 to 80, or 550 of 2700). The procedure as written is thus a different (and much more aggressive) algorithm than the one analyzed in Theorem thm:main_path and Remark rem:trimtiht-discussion.
issues.overall_effect: Mismatch between the stated procedure and the analyzed/experimented procedure; the analysis and the claimed equivalence 'Step 5 ... can be expressed as' only hold for the $m-m_{trim}$ version.
issues.title: TrimTIHT pseudocode keeps m_trim smallest rows, inconsistent with the trimmed-matrix definition used in the analysis
issues.why_classification: A single forced correction to the index set aligns the pseudocode with the definition and analysis without changing any result.

issues.failure_explanation: The quantities $\Delta_t,\rho_t,\xi_t,\mu_t,\|\mat A_t\|$ all depend on $t$. The proof establishes only the one-step contraction $\|\tR^{t+1}\|\le\alpha_t\|\tR^t\|$, which iterates to $\prod_{s\le t}\alpha_s\|\tR^0\|$, not to $\alpha_t^{\,t+1}\|\tR^0\|$ as stated; the stated bound can fail when earlier factors exceed the last one.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the $(t+1)$-th power by the product $\prod_{s=0}^{t}(\cdot)_s$ (or state the one-step bound).
issues.overall_effect: The displayed multi-step bound (eqn:conv_path) is not what is proved; the one-step bound and all discussion based on it remain valid.
issues.title: Theorem main_path states a (t+1)-th power of an iteration-dependent factor; proof gives a product
issues.why_classification: The forced correction is immediate from the proof and loses no content.

issues.failure_explanation: The simplification requires $\sqrt{2\xi_t+\xi_t^2}\,(1+\mu_t\|\mat A_t\|\sqrt{\Delta_t})\le|1-\mu_t\Delta_t|$. With $\xi_t\le\tfrac{16}{17}x^2/B^2$ ($x=|1-\mu_t\Delta_t|$, $B$ the bracket) one only gets $2\xi_t\le\tfrac{32}{17}x^2/B^2>x^2/B^2$, so the inequality fails; the implication holds with the Rauhut-type constant $1/17$ (then $2\xi+\xi^2\le(2/17+1/289)x^2/B^2<x^2/B^2$). The remark thus asserts an implication that is false under the condition it states.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the constant $16/17$ by $1/17$ (or any constant $c$ with $2c+c^2<1$) in the assumed bound on $\xi_t$.
issues.overall_effect: The simplified contraction factor $\alpha_t$ and the derived threshold ($\delta<0.106$ in the TensorRIP connection) are stated under an insufficient assumption on the thresholding accuracy.
issues.title: Remark's simplified rate (eqn:conv_path_err) does not follow from the stated xi_t condition with constant 16/17
issues.why_classification: Correcting one constant restores the implication with the same conclusion.
